title: November 2nd the People That We Want to Be with a Saga of Pornstar Tears Korean
description: The public-facing finale of the November 2 event combines a DVDASA fan wedding, Mangchi concert, giveaways, audience stories and an increasingly explicit question-and-answer session.
summary: The public-facing finale of the November 2 event combines a DVDASA fan wedding, Mangchi concert, giveaways, audience stories and an increasingly explicit question-and-answer session. David Choe opens after roughly a day awake by arguing that relentless effort can make supposedly doomed projects work, then applies the idea—uneasily—to marriage. He officiates for the fan handles Broken Sketchbook 69 and Delma 69, with the DVDASA community as witness. The ceremony contains sincere testimony about meeting through the show alongside sexual spectacle and crowd pressure; the archive preserves the former without treating a stage wedding as proof of civil registration or publishing the couple's private identities. Bobby Lee, Steve Lee, Asa Akira, Critter Fleming, Bobby Trivia, Money Mark and other public participants thank the audience before Mangchi performs a long, rough set. The musical section includes anti-bullying themes, songs about alienation and sex, onstage fatigue, crowd interaction and decoder-damaged lyrics that are not silently upgraded into exact quotations. The later giveaway and audience segments are as important as the concert. Travelers and creative collaborators describe meeting through DVDASA, surviving setbacks and competing while remaining friendly. Fans ask about art, relationships, sex and show history. The room repeatedly crosses boundaries: people are asked whether they are gay, intimate acts are solicited, an audience member says ‘don't touch me,’ and private breakup distress becomes live material. Those objections and vulnerability remain part of the summary rather than disappearing behind a celebratory fan-event label. The title phrase lands near the end when David identifies the gathered audience as the people he wants to be with. It is a statement of chosen community after a difficult production day, not a claim that every interaction was safe. The people list corrects stable public names but does not convert crowd members, fan handles or joking identities into searchable biographies. This is an automatic, non-diarized transcript of a visually dense performance; source video is required for exact cast, actions, lyrics and attribution.
